title: View from Olympus
subject: greek-mythology
author: Clueberry Desk
introduction: The household on the mountain, as the poets tell it: portfolios, attributes and one very long-running grudge.
completionMessage: The council is seated. Grid closed.

entries.clue: Sprung fully armed from her father's head
entries.explanation: In the myth she is born from the head of the sky-god, already wearing armour.
Lame in most versions of the story, and the maker of the gods' finest metalwork.
Both are children of Leto in the standard genealogy.

entries.clue: Bird that shadowed the goddess of wisdom
entries.explanation: Its little owl became the emblem of Athens along with her.

entries.clue: Wronged queen of the Olympian household
entries.explanation: Goddess of marriage in the myths, and the one most often kept in the dark.

entries.clue: Earth-shaker of the sea, in myth
entries.explanation: "Earth-shaker" is his standing epithet in Homer; earthquakes were credited to him.

entries.clue: Tree offered to Athens, according to legend
entries.explanation: In the contest for the city, the sea-god struck out salt water and the wisdom goddess produced this tree; the city chose the tree.
The instrument is also Apollo's, given to him by Hermes in the myth.

factCards.text: In Hesiod's Theogony, the Olympians take power only after a ten-year war against the Titans. The poem, composed around 700 BCE, is one of the oldest written sources for the whole family tree.
There is no single canonical list of twelve Olympians. Ancient authors and sanctuaries swap figures such as Hestia, Dionysus and Hades in and out, so different sources count a different twelve.
Athena's owl and olive sprig appear together with her helmeted profile on Athenian silver coins of the fifth century BCE — myth used as state branding.
